chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: Leg circulation problems and bypass surgery
summary: Circulation trouble discovered in Europe led to bypass surgery and a slow return to playing.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: When did you start having the physical trouble?

Oh, that was last year. That's when my legs started to hurt. Then I went to Senior Citizens Clinic uptown, and I ran across this doctor there, a (?) doctor... Anyway, she was telling me that she knew an Indian doctor that was very good at ...(?)...
Because they realized that was circulation, it was coming from the heart.
Yeah, that it was coming from the heart. So they figured that's what I needed. And it really was what I needed. Thank goodness she had the insight to know where it was coming from.
She diagnosed it correctly.

She knew that's what it was. Because I couldn't walk for three blocks without my legs hurting, man. And you know what that is? Pshew! I mean hurting. I don't mean just a pain hit you and everything. I mean, this was just hurting. If I had any distance to walk, I'm in
McGhee (12/1) - 36

trouble. I first felt it when I was over in Europe. I was walking, and then one day it started to hurt. I figured there was something wrong. I said, "This ain't right." I thought maybe it was the shoes that I was wearing or something that was causing the legs to hurt, but it wasn't that. It's just that there was no circulation in my legs. Which they corrected, thank goodness.
So you went in and had the bypass.

Yeah. I went to Metropolitan, and they operated on me, and they put in two new veins, one in each leg, all the way up to the top of my stomach. And it's been kind of rough, because in that same time my teeth got bad and I had to have some new teeth made.
Everything happens at once.

Yeah. Well, I'm glad it all happened at once rather than this and then that and then something else... And it will help me get myself back together physically and healthy... Health-wise, I got my health. But it took a little while for me to realize that it takes a long time to heal when you get split open. Because it really is. When they split you open, boy oh boy...
I didn't know I would have all of those kind of problems when I went to see about it. I didn't even know the process of what they do when your legs start to hurt.
McGhee (12/1) - 37
But since then it's been pretty good. I try not to... If I walk a lot, it don't bother me. But if I lay around and don't take exercise...
So exercise is very important.
Very important to your legs.
Naturally, you didn't play all that time.
Well, you couldn't play with...
You couldn't play, no... So then you had to gradually start.

Just gradually start coming back and trying to play. I'll be working around town. I'll play out at the Island for a couple of days, starting the 17th or 18th, and then I'll play the 26th here at the Church.
Is this the first you've played in a while in public?

Yeah. Well, it's been quite a while, yeah. I played All Souls Night down at the Church, but I didn't play that much. But I just (?) enough to keep a little time. But I will be playing down at Sonny's Place; I know you ain't goin' way out there.
Out in Seaford, huh?
Yeah.
But how do your chops feel now?
Well, they're coming along pretty good. I've been playing a lot (?) work until they get precise, and
McGhee (12/1) - 38
then I think they'll be all right. But everything is coming along pretty good.
Are you doing any writing?
Oh yeah. Well, I always do that, since I learned how to play music I've been trying to learn how to write.
